newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Tribal leader shot dead in Bangladesh Hill Tracts.
newsitem.headline: Tribal leader shot dead in Bangladesh Hill Tracts.

text.p: Tribal leader Adi Shankar Khisa was shot dead by suspected separatists in Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts, police said on Friday.
They said Khisa, a local council chairman, was sprayed with bullets on Thursday night while returning home from a police station in Khagrachhari hill town.
Police said they believed Khisa was disliked by the tribal Shanti Bahini, comprising mostly Chakma tribesmen, for trying to negotiate a peace deal with the government.
"The Shanti Bahini is the prime suspect (in Khisa's killing), but we are investigating," one police officer said.
Another tribal peace promoter, Subinoy Chakma, was gunned down by suspected Shanti Bahini guerrillas near his home in Rangamati hill town on December 25, police said.
Subinoy was secretary-general of Chittagong Hill Tracts National Coordination and Peace Council.

The Shanti Bahini has fought a bush war for autonomy of the 5,500 sq miles (14,200 sq km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, since 1973. Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency.
They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
